$ ergon release --help
Usage: ergon release <command> [options]

Plan, write and publish the releases of the packages of the repository.

ergon release releases the packages of the repository with the changesets of
.changeset and the configuration .changeset/config.json, in the format of
changesets: a pull request adds a changeset that names the packages it changes
with their bumps, the version pull request writes the new versions and the
changelogs, and its merge publishes and tags the packages. The packages are the
packages that each toolchain of ergon discovers, such as the modules of go.work.

Commands:
  add           Add a changeset.
  status        Report the changes of the branch that no changeset releases.
  version       Write the new versions, the requirements and the changelogs.
  publish-plan  Write the packages that a publish uploads or tags.
  pack          Build the artifacts of the packages of a publish plan.
  publish       Publish and tag the packages of a publish plan.
  sign          Sign and publish the drafts of the providers of the Terraform Registry.
  git-tag       Tag the packages whose tags are missing.
  ci            Run the jobs of the release workflow.

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

Global options:

      --version     Show the version.

$ ergon release ci --help
Usage: ergon release ci <command> [options]

Run the jobs of the release workflow.

ergon release ci runs the steps of the jobs of the release workflows and of the
first job of ci.yml in GitHub Actions, and writes their outputs into the file
of GITHUB_OUTPUT.

Commands:
  select-mode  Choose the job that the release workflow runs.
  skip         Decide whether a CI run skips its jobs.
  verify       Verify that a CI run passed on the content of the commit.
  version      Write the release and open the version pull request.
  homebrew     Commit the casks of a publish to the Homebrew tap.

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon release add --help
Usage: ergon release add [options]

Add a changeset.

ergon release add writes a changeset into .changeset: the packages that --bump
names, each with its bump, and the summary of --message as the entry of their
changelogs. --empty writes a changeset without packages, which satisfies ergon
release status for a change that releases nothing. --open opens the changeset
in the editor of VISUAL or EDITOR after it writes it.

Example:
  ergon release add --bump go.dokimi.dev/ergon/core=minor -m "Add the Unit type."

Options:
      --bump string,...  Release of a package, as name=level, where level is major, minor, patch or none.  env ERGON_RELEASE_ADD_BUMP
      --empty            Write a changeset without packages.                                               env ERGON_RELEASE_ADD_EMPTY
  -m, --message string   Summary of the changeset.                                                         env ERGON_RELEASE_ADD_MESSAGE
      --open             Open the changeset in the editor.                                                 env ERGON_RELEASE_ADD_OPEN

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon release status --help
Usage: ergon release status [options]

Report the changes of the branch that no changeset releases.

ergon release status writes the release plan of the changesets that the branch
added since --since, the base branch by default. It reports each package that
the branch changed without a changeset that names it, and each requirement of a
package on another package of the repository that excludes the current version
of the other. The exit status is 1 when it reports either. --output writes the
plan as JSON into a file.

Options:
      --output string  File that receives the release plan as JSON.            env ERGON_RELEASE_STATUS_OUTPUT
      --since string   Commit to compare against, the base branch by default.  env ERGON_RELEASE_STATUS_SINCE
      --verbose        List the changesets of each release.                    env ERGON_RELEASE_STATUS_VERBOSE

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon release version --help
Usage: ergon release version [options]

Write the new versions, the requirements and the changelogs.

ergon release version writes the release plan of the changesets into the
repository: the new version of each package, the rewritten requirements of its
dependents, the entries of the changelogs and the refreshed lockfiles. It
removes the changesets that it consumed, and restores every file when a step
fails. Without changesets it rewrites the lockfiles that record the earlier
content of a package whose release waits for its publish. --dry-run writes the
plan and changes nothing.

Options:
      --dry-run  Write the release plan and change nothing.  env ERGON_RELEASE_VERSION_DRY_RUN

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon release publish-plan --help
Usage: ergon release publish-plan [options]

Write the packages that a publish uploads or tags.

ergon release publish-plan writes the publish plan as JSON: each package whose
registry lacks its version, and each package whose tag is its release and is
missing, in chunks of dependency order. --output writes the plan into a file.

Options:
      --output string  File that receives the publish plan.  env ERGON_RELEASE_PUBLISH_PLAN_OUTPUT

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon release pack --help
Usage: ergon release pack [options]

Build the artifacts of the packages of a publish plan.

ergon release pack builds the artifacts of each package of the publish plan
into --out-dir: the files that its registry receives, and the assets of its
release under assets/<tag>/, such as the archives, the packages and the
checksums of the commands of a Go module, which GoReleaser builds and signs.

Options:
      --from-publish-plan string  File that contains the publish plan.    env ERGON_RELEASE_PACK_FROM_PUBLISH_PLAN
      --out-dir string            Directory that receives the artifacts.  default "dist", env ERGON_RELEASE_PACK_OUT_DIR

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon release publish --help
Usage: ergon release publish [options]

Publish and tag the packages of a publish plan.

ergon release publish uploads each package of the publish plan whose registry
lacks its version, and then tags each package at HEAD with the section of its
changelog as the notes. On a workstation it creates annotated tags and pushes
them to origin in one push. In GitHub Actions it creates the tags and the
GitHub Releases through the API of GitHub: each release as a draft, then its
assets from assets/<tag>/ of --from-pack-dir, and then the publish of the
draft. A run after a failed upload completes the draft. A release with the file
drafts/<tag> in --from-pack-dir remains a draft, which ergon release sign signs
and publishes. It refuses a plan whose lockfiles record other content of its
packages than the working tree, and on a workstation a release with assets.
--no-git-tag creates no tag.

Options:
      --from-pack-dir string      Directory of the artifacts to upload.              default "dist", env ERGON_RELEASE_PUBLISH_FROM_PACK_DIR
      --from-publish-plan string  File that contains the publish plan.               env ERGON_RELEASE_PUBLISH_FROM_PUBLISH_PLAN
      --no-git-tag                Do not create a tag.                               env ERGON_RELEASE_PUBLISH_NO_GIT_TAG
      --output string             File that receives the released packages as JSON.  env ERGON_RELEASE_PUBLISH_OUTPUT

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon release sign --help
Usage: ergon release sign [options]

Sign and publish the drafts of the providers of the Terraform Registry.

ergon release sign completes each draft release of the repository of
GITHUB_REPOSITORY that waits for a signature, or each draft of --tag. A draft
waits for a signature when its tag is v<version> and it has the checksums
<name>_<version>_SHA256SUMS, which ergon release publish leaves for a provider
of the Terraform Registry. The cosign of the section go checks the bundle of the
checksums against the release workflow of the base branch at the commit of the
tag, and ergon release sign checks the digest of each asset of the draft
against the checksums. The gpg of the PATH then signs the checksums with the key
of the fingerprint --key, and the agent of gpg asks for the PIN of the key.
ergon release sign checks the signature, uploads it and publishes the draft.
GITHUB_TOKEN needs write access to the contents of the repository, and the
Terraform Registry accepts a key of the type RSA or DSA.

Example:
  GITHUB_REPOSITORY=example/terraform-provider-demo GITHUB_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)" \
    ergon release sign --key 0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF01234567

Options:
      --key string      Fingerprint of the GPG key that signs the checksums.  required, env ERGON_RELEASE_SIGN_KEY
      --tag string,...  Tag of a draft to sign, once for each draft.          env ERGON_RELEASE_SIGN_TAG

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon release git-tag --help
Usage: ergon release git-tag [options]

Tag the packages whose tags are missing.

ergon release git-tag creates the annotated tag of each package whose tag at
its version is missing, at HEAD, and pushes the tags to origin in one push. It
refuses a plan whose lockfiles record other content of its packages than the
working tree.

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon release ci select-mode --help
Usage: ergon release ci select-mode [options]

Choose the job that the release workflow runs.

ergon release ci select-mode writes the mode of the release workflow: version
for changesets that release a package or for lockfiles that record the earlier
content of a package of the publish plan, publish for a publish plan with a
package, and none otherwise. It writes each such lockfile. --output writes the
publish plan into a file for the job publish.

Options:
      --output string  File that receives the publish plan.  env ERGON_RELEASE_CI_SELECT_MODE_OUTPUT

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon release ci skip --help
Usage: ergon release ci skip [options]

Decide whether a CI run skips its jobs.

ergon release ci skip writes the output skip of the first job of ci.yml: true
when a passed run of the workflow --workflow already covers the content of the
checkout, and false otherwise, through the API of GitHub. A run of a push skips
when a run passed on its content, as ergon release ci verify finds it. A run
skips when its commit is a version commit, which ergon release ci version marks
with the status ergon/version, and a run passed on the parent of that commit.
--commit names the head of a pull request, whose checkout merges it into its
base. Without GITHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_REPOSITORY, and on an error of GitHub, it
writes a warning and false, so that the run tests the commit.

Options:
      --commit string    Commit to test, such as the head of a pull request.  env ERGON_RELEASE_CI_SKIP_COMMIT
      --workflow string  Workflow file whose passed runs count.               default "ci.yml", env ERGON_RELEASE_CI_SKIP_WORKFLOW

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon release ci verify --help
Usage: ergon release ci verify [options]

Verify that a CI run passed on the content of the commit.

ergon release ci verify finds a run of the workflow --workflow that passed on the
content of the commit of HEAD, through the API of GitHub: a run of the commit
itself, such as the run of its push or of its merge group, or a run of the head
of a pull request that merged the commit with the same tree. It reads each run
once and waits for none. The exit status is 1 without such a run.

Options:
      --workflow string  Workflow file whose passed runs count.  default "ci.yml", env ERGON_RELEASE_CI_VERIFY_WORKFLOW

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon release ci version --help
Usage: ergon release ci version [options]

Write the release and open the version pull request.

ergon release ci version writes the release plan of the changesets as ergon
release version does. It then commits the changes on the branch
ergon-release/<base> through the API of GitHub, which signs the commits, and
opens or updates the version pull request into the base branch. It marks the
head of the branch with the status ergon/version, with which ergon release ci
skip recognises the version commit. Without a changeset that releases a
package it proposes the lockfiles that ergon release version rewrites, and
otherwise changes nothing. Changesets at none or without packages wait for the
next release. It skips a commit of HEAD that is no longer the head of the base
branch, and leaves the pull request to the run of the newer head.

Options:
      --title string  Title of the pull request and of its commits.  default "chore: version packages", env ERGON_RELEASE_CI_VERSION_TITLE

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon release ci homebrew --help
Usage: ergon release ci homebrew [options]

Commit the casks of a publish to the Homebrew tap.

ergon release ci homebrew commits each cask that ergon release pack wrote for a
release of the publish plan, casks/<tag>/<name>.rb of --from-pack-dir, to
Casks/<name>.rb of the tap --tap, through the API of GitHub with the token of
GITHUB_TOKEN, which needs write access to the contents of the tap. Each cask is
one commit, which GitHub signs, and a cask that the tap already has is no
commit.

Example:
  ergon release ci homebrew --tap dokimasia/homebrew-tap --from-publish-plan publish-plan.json

Options:
      --from-pack-dir string      Directory of the casks.                      default "dist", env ERGON_RELEASE_CI_HOMEBREW_FROM_PACK_DIR
      --from-publish-plan string  File that contains the publish plan.         env ERGON_RELEASE_CI_HOMEBREW_FROM_PUBLISH_PLAN
      --tap string                Tap that receives the casks, as owner/name.  required, env ERGON_RELEASE_CI_HOMEBREW_TAP

Global options:
      --flag-debug  Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env ERGON_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help        Show the help.
      --version     Show the version.
[exit 0]

$ ergon release add
ergon: cli: name the packages with --bump, or pass --empty
[exit 2]

$ ergon release add --bump example.com/demo -m x
ergon: cli: --bump "example.com/demo", which is not <name>=<major|minor|patch|none>
[exit 2]

$ ergon release add --bump example.com/demo=huge -m x
ergon: cli: --bump "example.com/demo=huge", which is not <name>=<major|minor|patch|none>
[exit 2]

$ ergon release ci homebrew
ergon: release ci homebrew: missing --tap
[exit 2]

$ ergon release sign
ergon: release sign: missing --key
[exit 2]

$ ergon release sign --key ABC123
ergon: cli: --key "ABC123", which is not the fingerprint of a GPG key
[exit 2]

$ ergon release sign --key GGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGG
ergon: cli: --key "GGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGG", which is not the fingerprint of a GPG key
[exit 2]
